analyst_view.overall: Athletic (7th, 16 pts) host Espanyol (13th, 12 pts) on Friday night at San Mamés, the first game after the international break. Edin Terzic's Athletic have a thin back line: Vivian (soleus) and Paredes are out, both already in the numbers, and Laporte and Unai Simón were still managing their load on Tuesday after national-team duty; Guruzeta and Sannadi are out up front, but Nico Williams is back in group training. Espanyol changed coach at the end of October: Eder Sarabia replaced Manolo González (one point from his last fifteen league games) and wants a possession side that builds from the back, a big change from Manolo's deep block; his only game so far was a 0-0 with Deportivo. Espanyol still miss Kike García and Urko González, Jofre Carreras is nursing an adductor problem, and Edu Expósito trained apart on Wednesday with an unspecified knock, which the numbers do not know about. No referee has been named.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already take off about 8% of Athletic's scoring for Paredes and some of Espanyol's for their weak scoring run (4 goals in 6). Athletic's defence is shaky with Vivian and Paredes out and Laporte not fully back, which helps Espanyol a little, but Espanyol may lose Edu Expósito, their main creator, and still have no Kike García. Those pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 2.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners, 6.4 of them Athletic's, and already add Athletic's recent corner count against an Espanyol side that conceded 44 in six games. Nico Williams back on the wing keeps Athletic's usual wide game at San Mamés. Sarabia wants Espanyol to keep the ball more, but one game is too little to say they will concede fewer corners, so I keep 10.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards and add about 9% for Espanyol's heavy card run (20 in six games), almost all of it under Manolo González's deep, combative side. Sarabia's team is built to keep the ball and press higher, which usually means fewer fouls from chasing the game, and his debut against Deportivo was a calm 0-0. No referee is named yet, so this is a mild trim to about 4.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots, with Athletic taking 17.7, and already add Athletic's busy recent shooting (94 in six games). Athletic are short of a central striker with Guruzeta and Sannadi out, but Nico and Iñaki Williams carry most of the shooting anyway. Espanyol's new possession plan could cut Athletic's share a little, but there is not enough evidence yet, so I keep 26.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target and already take a bit off Espanyol for their weak recent finishing (18 on target in six). Edu Expósito's doubt and Kike García's absence keep Espanyol's threat low, while Athletic's attack is close to full strength with Nico Williams back. Nothing the numbers miss clearly moves it, so 8.4.
